evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.reasoning: Mission concept, users, and national need for Great Barrier Reef monitoring are clearly defined and referenced. Technical specifications and quantitative requirements could be more thoroughly detailed.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.reasoning: A Gantt chart is included and mapped out. However, the plan lacks risk/contingency considerations, planned future information sources are not listed, and orbital physics logic is flawed.
No actual preliminary mission design results, hand calculations, or STK outputs are presented beyond completing general tutorials.
The report is clearly structured, readable, and includes a well-formatted Gantt chart. However, footnotes are raw URLs without full bibliographic details, and figures lack formal captions.

technical_issues.issue: A geostationary orbit cannot physically exist at an altitude of 600 km (geostationary altitude is ~35,786 km above the equator). A 600 km orbit is Low Earth Orbit (LEO) with a ~96-minute period.

overall: Good mission rationale for Australia. However, preliminary technical work is missing, planned information sources are absent, and asserting a 600 km geostationary orbit represents a major orbital mechanics error.
